rationale: Tests spatial identification of the six respiratory chain components whose order and membrane location are the core visual learning point of block 5.
Tests recall of chemiosmotic theory terms and P:O ratios that complete the oxidative phosphorylation mechanism in block 6.
Tests understanding of the central metabolic hubs and the irreversibility of the pyruvate-to-acetyl-CoA step, the core integration concept completed in block 9.
Tests understanding of the temporal progression of metabolic states from fed through prolonged starvation, the hormonal switching concept completed in block 11.
Tests recall of the four classes of mitochondrial disruptors and their key agents, completing the energy-failure learning point in block 13.
Tests recall of macronutrient energy values and the mutual supplementation principle that are the core dietary-science learning points of block 4.

Tests understanding of the ordered steps of the visual cycle, the mechanism linking vitamin A to night vision and explaining why night blindness is the earliest deficiency symptom, as taught in block 7.
Tests understanding of the sequential activation of vitamin D through skin, liver and kidney, and why chronic kidney disease causes rickets despite adequate sunlight, as taught in block 8.
Tests recall of the clinical presentations and key rules for thiamine and niacin deficiency, completing the beriberi–Wernicke's–pellagra learning point in block 12.
Tests the ability to discriminate findings specific to vitamin B12 deficiency from features shared with folate deficiency, the critical clinical discrimination completed in block 13.
Tests the ability to distinguish marasmus from kwashiorkor by their defining clinical features and the VLDL mechanism of fatty liver, completing the PEM learning point in block 18.
Tests recall of Indian-specific BMI cutoffs, waist circumference thresholds and metabolic syndrome diagnostic criteria from block 19.
